name: OK-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean in western Oklahoma
Long-serving incumbent Frank Lucas with a massive financial edge ($1.0M raised vs. $18K)
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 96-97%
No polls or expert ratings indicate any competitive threat
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Lucas: a deeply Republican district, decades of incumbency, and a lopsided fundraising gap over an underfunded challenger. Markets and the absence of any competitive signals corroborate a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or a dramatic national wave against Republicans would put this seat in play, and even then the margin makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 3rd District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and Frank Lucas has held it since the 1990s. He enters the general election with more than $1 million raised and over $575,000 on hand, while Democrat Suzie Byrd has raised about $18,000. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets put Lucas's chances above 95%.

The fundamentals favor Lucas on every measurable front: the district's strong partisan lean, his long incumbency, and the lopsided money gap. Byrd would need an extraordinary shift in the political environment to make the race competitive, and nothing in the available evidence suggests one is underway. The seat is rated Safe R.
